title: A non-interventional prospective study investigating long-term use of Daruph in adult patients with BCR::ABL1-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia in the chronic phase (CML-CP) in a real-life setting
summary:
This study is a non-interventional observational study in patients with chronic myelogenous leukemia in the chronic phase (CML-CP), who receive routine treatment with Daruph.

CML is a slowly progressing cancer that affects the blood and bone marrow. Daruph has recently received market authorisation in Germany to treat CML-CP. It can be absorbed better and faster by the body compared to similar medications. Further, the formulation of Daruph allows patients to take addtional medication to reduce stomach discomfort. 

The aim of this observational study is to investigate the long-term use of Daruph in the CML-CP population, primarily to assess maintenance of Daruph treatment, but also to describe treatment response, treatment safety, concomitant treatments, dose modifications, and patient quality of life and treatment satisfaction.
conditions: Chronic myeloid leukemia, BCR/ABL-positive, not having achieved remission

interventions.name:
Observation group:

Patients with BCR::ABL1-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia in the chronic phase (CML-CP), who receive routine treatment with Daruph

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Adult patients of 18 years or older at index date
• A clinical diagnosis of CML-CP with confirmed BCR::ABL1 positivity
• Started treatment with Daruph, or switched to Daruph from another dasatinib formulation, according to label and local market reimbursement no more than 6 months before enrolment
• Able and willing to read and comprehend written instructions
• Have provided written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Diagnosed with CML in the blast phase (CML-BP)
• Previously received another dasatinib formulation for > 6 months prior to Daruph treatment
• Has dasatinib-resistant mutations
• Participating in an ongoing interventional trial
